hooks.text: Shortly before 10 a.m., New York’s tallest skyscraper vanished into fog.
A B-25 bomber pilot was flying blind through the Manhattan fog.
An elevator operator survived falling 75 stories inside a metal box.

title: The B-25 That Struck the Empire State Building 🤯
description: In 1945, a lost US Army bomber crashed into the Empire State Building, leading to one of history's most miraculous survival stories.

beats.text: Shortly before 10 a.m., New York’s tallest skyscraper vanished into fog.
beats.visual: Empire State Building shrouded in thick fog, 1945.

beats.text: Colonel William Smith steered his B-25 bomber toward Midtown Manhattan.
beats.visual: B-25 Mitchell bomber aircraft in flight, 1945.

beats.text: Flying at 200 miles per hour, the plane struck the 79th floor.
beats.visual: North face of the Empire State Building showing impact damage, 1945.
queries: Empire State Building B-25 crash hole 1945

beats.text: One engine plummeted down a shaft, severing the heavy elevator cables.
beats.visual: Wreckage of the B-25 inside an office on the 79th floor, 1945.

beats.text: Rescuers placed injured operator Betty Lou Oliver into a car to evacuate her.
beats.visual: Portrait of survivor Betty Lou Oliver in uniform, 1945.

beats.text: The cables snapped, plunging her 75 stories into the subbasement.
beats.visual: View down the damaged elevator shaft of the Empire State Building, 1945.
queries: Empire State Building elevator shaft crash 1945

beats.text: A cushion of trapped air saved her life from the impossible fall.
beats.visual: Front page of the New York Daily News regarding the crash, 1945.
queries: New York Daily News July 29 1945 Empire State crash
Empire State Building plane crash newspaper

beats.text: She survived the morning the tallest skyscraper vanished into fog.
beats.visual: The spire of the Empire State Building rising through the clouds, 1945.

better_than_last: The countdown structure creates higher tension by moving from the atmospheric fog directly into the collision and the miraculous survival of Betty Lou Oliver.
